item.description:
Saturday, October 17 | Doors: 6 pm | Show: 7:30 pm | From $36.30 Event Details and Tickets
Celebrate 20 years since their inception, the ground-breaking, Grammy Award-winning ensemble The Infamous Stringdusters—whose tone and swagger meld acoustic majesty with the energy of a full-blown rock show—mark this milestone with the release of 20/20. Twenty brand new songs, born from endless miles in pursuit of a dream. Formed in Nashville in the early 2000s while performing as side-men with stalwarts of the bluegrass community, the band members soaked up every influence like musical sponges. Their friendships, paired with a shared drive to create their own music and master their own destiny, inevitably led to the birth of The Infamous Stringdusters. Alongside Chris Pandolfi (banjo), Travis Book (double bass), Jeremy Garrett (fiddle), Andy Hall (dobro), and Andy Falco (guitar), the group continues to fearlessly blur the boundaries between bluegrass, Americana, country, and indie-folk.

item.title: Jack’s Old-Time Jam — Wed Oct 14, 5:00 PM — Jack Of The Wood
item.description:
Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. The venue extends a welcoming feeling to regulars and newcomers to this day. https://jackofthewood.com/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: "Lost Ground: America's Landslide Crisis" Film Screening — Wed Oct 14, 6:30 PM
item.description:
UNC Asheville will be screening the recent documentary “Lost Ground: America’s Landslide Crisis” in Mullen & James Humanities Hall. The screening is to be followed by a panel discussion and Q&A moderated by the director, WCNC’s investigative reporter Nate Morabito. The panelists include:
Paige Ambord and Caitlin Meagher, faculty in the Department of Sociology and Anthropology and who are featured in the film for their work on landslide survivors post-Helene Jackie Langille, an expert on landslide geography in the Department of Environmental Science.
This important film exposes the extent of landslide damage during Helene, and raises awareness of landslide risks, two years after that devastating event.

item.title: Jam > Grass > Jam: The Saylor Brothers — Wed Oct 14, 6:30 PM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
The Saylor Brothers are a jamgrass fusion group from Asheville, fronted by brothers Will & Ben Saylor, of Brushfire Stankgrass. This project is a foray further into the realm of bluegrass jam, with more emphasis on improvisation piled on top of a structure of traditional bluegrass and innovative original songwriting. As a trio with Greg Stiglets on bass, the band packs a large sound coming from three acoustic instruments, and often adds a fourth player for further improvisational and bluegrass firepower.
Jam > Grass > Jam is not an open bluegrass jam but is a residency featuring a rotating casts of special guests from Asheville’s bluegrass/jamband scene.
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. item.description:
Awakening Asheville Are you tantalized by different healing modalities? Do you thrive on community magic?
Join us for an opportunity to give of your gifts along with a group to another, and then receive the menagerie offered you! Practice asking for what you want and need and trusting that the collective efforts will heal/launch you into an never-before-felt-experience of group focus…on loving YOU!
Some examples of previous offerings: reiki, activations, massage, crystals and gem stone magic, didgeridoo and other sound healing, and oracle card draws. We have some instruments that you are welcome to play such as crystal bowls, drums, handpans, rainsticks, etc.
Our event has been described by our community member Lauren as “Wow! Experimental play, multi-sensory, multidimensional, intuitive energy, and sound magic healing.”
Some fellowship with snacks afterwards. Bring some if you're inspired!

item.description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

item.title: Shut Up & Write!® in Candler/West Asheville — Mon Nov 2, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Please join me and other local writers for a group writing session. Bring whatever you're working on and grab a coffee, and we will write alongside each other.
This is not a critique group, but we do have short social periods before and after writing. \-\-\- Many have mentioned that The Dripolator is a little hard to find if you've never been before. The coffeeshop is located in a strip mall where the Candler YMCA is, and the sonic. The Dripolator is next to the bank, and looks a little like a house. There is usually plenty of parking in the lot out front. If you're having trouble send me a message!
Source: Shut Up & Write Western NC

item.title: Fun & easy way to play more tennis (please read event description for details) — Thu Nov 5, 7:00 PM
item.description:
PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis We’re still working to get more people into these Meetups, but our goal is to give PlayYourCourt members a few social tennis outings each week in addition to your practice sessions and Challenge League matches.
These Meetups are co-ed, super laid back, and all skill levels are welcome. Post your skill level and a suggested court in the comments section so we can round up as many players as we can for some tennis fun!
Also, if you’re looking to meet new practice partners or play some matches and you aren’t already in the PlayYourCourt Community, you can go here to see what we’re all about and sign up:
https://www.playyourcourt.com/tennis-community/asheville-nc/meetup/
If you love tennis, we’d love to have you! Be sure and watch the quick video that explains how everything works.
Happy hitting!
- Scott
Source: PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis

item.title: Come sing with us! Vocal workshop and rehearsal - Land Of The Sky Chorus — Tue Nov 10, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Asheville Area A Cappella Singers Whether you are an experienced singer, or just like to sing in your car, come join us as our guest! The Land of The Sky Chorus, located in Asheville, NC, is welcoming guests - men and women - who are interested in joining us in the world-wide community of a cappella singing.
No experience is required; we provide music, voice training and an enjoyable singing experience under expert leadership. Our repertoire of music is fun and spans many styles - most songs are easy to learn and sing. Learning materials are provided to help you get started, and you will be paired with a singing "Buddy" so you can join in right away.
We will be here to greet you as early as 6:15pm to help you get situated.
Source: Asheville Area A Cappella Singers
